socTitle: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators

onet.title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
onet.description: Operate or control an entire process or system of machines, often through the use of control boards, to transfer or treat water or wastewater.

task.title: Collect and test water and sewage samples, using test equipment and color analysis standards.
Operate and adjust controls on equipment to purify and clarify water, process or dispose of sewage, and generate power.
Record operational data, personnel attendance, or meter and gauge readings on specified forms.
Add chemicals, such as ammonia, chlorine, or lime, to disinfect and deodorize water and other liquids.
Inspect equipment or monitor operating conditions, meters, and gauges to determine load requirements and detect malfunctions.
Direct and coordinate plant workers engaged in routine operations and maintenance activities.
Clean and maintain tanks, filter beds, and other work areas, using hand tools and power tools.
Maintain, repair, and lubricate equipment, using hand tools and power tools.
Complete wastewater discharge monitoring reports and maintenance logs.
Maintain and repair portable safety equipment and permanent safety infrastructure to ensure operational readiness and compliance with safety protocols.

activity.title: Collect samples of materials or products for testing.
Test chemical or physical characteristics of materials or products.
Operate chemical processing or water treatment systems or equipment.

trades.description: A Wastewater Systems Operation Specialist runs and monitors the equipment that moves and cleans sewage at treatment plants and pump stations. They test water, adjust chemical levels, inspect pipes and tanks, record readings, and fix or report problems. Their work keeps wastewater systems running properly and protects public health, waterways, and the environment.

trades.description: A Water Systems Operation Specialist runs and maintains the equipment that moves, treats, and stores drinking water and wastewater. They check gauges, test water samples, adjust pumps and valves, inspect pipes and tanks, and respond to system problems. Their work keeps water clean, pressure steady, and essential public systems running safely every day.
